title: I Let the Customer Keep the Rule About Twenty Minutes

parts.text: I scanned the last garden gnome at 8:41 p.m. and she slapped a coupon on the belt. We closed at nine. The laminated sign said no returns or price matches in the final twenty minutes. She wanted both. I am twenty-four, morning barista, night cashier. "Policy," I said, tapping the sign. She smiled with all her teeth. "Your manager makes exceptions for loyal customers." Craig was hiding in receiving with Flamin' Hot Cheetos. The bag crinkled over the walkie. "Craig," I radioed. "Price match and a return. Eight forty-one." He answered, mouth full: "Honor the sign. No exceptions." She heard it. The line heard it. She planted her purse on the scanner. "Then I stand here until nine-oh-one." A kid in the next cart spun a fidget, click click click. The belt smelled like wet cardboard and a broken cinnamon candle. I locked my register and killed the light. "Ma'am, you are correct. We are inside the twenty. I cannot help you until we are not." Her visor twitched. "That's not what I meant." Craig hissed, "Do not lock that till." I already had. She leaned in. "Priya. I will have your job." I nodded. "After nine. Until then, per your rule, I am closed." The doors kept cycling. The gnome smiled its painted smile like it knew I had given her the next twenty minutes of her life.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Register locked, Craig yelling, and she is blocking the scanner until the clock hits her own loophole.

social.description: A visor, a garden gnome, and a closing policy she wanted both sides of. I locked the till inside the twenty minutes she quoted. Would you have kept the line waiting?

parts.text: The doors kept opening for Craig, Cheeto dust on his polo, trying to look like leadership. "Unlock it," he said. I pointed at the sign and at her. "She invoked the twenty minutes. You said honor the sign." Someone started recording. The woman said, "I want a manager who isn't you." Craig smiled at the phone. "We can make an exception." I said, "You radioed no exceptions." I held the walkie and replayed it. Our cheap radios keep a six-second buffer if you hold the side button. Craig's voice said honor the sign. She went red under the visor. At 9:00:17 I unlocked, rang the gnome at regular price, and declined the expired coupon because expired is expired. She shoved it back. "I don't want it." I voided on camera. Craig tried to comp a candle. I scanned the broken cinnamon one. "Damaged inventory. I can't sell it." He overrode my register. District emailed in the morning with the phone video attached, Cheeto orange and contradictions. They moved the twenty-minute sign to the entrance and added: managers may not override audio they created. She posted that I was rude. The gnome sits by the time clock in employee holds. I tap its hat when I clock out. Craig eats Cheetos in his car now. I will take that as progress.

social.video_title: The radio replayed his own order — Part 2/2
social.description: Craig wanted an exception after telling me not to make one. The six-second buffer on a cheap walkie did more than a complaint form. Was the gnome even worth it?
